# TomoKV — project context for codex

Prepend this to every codex prompt. It is the shared background; each prompt then states its own scope.
Written 2026-09-07. Baseline commit `78c3e5391` (`origin/cpp`), full gate 344/344.

## What it is

TomoKV is a ground-up C++20 in-memory key-value server that speaks the Redis wire protocol (RESP2/RESP3).
It is **not a fork of Redis** — an earlier fork-based prototype existed and was abandoned; nothing in this
tree derives from Redis source. It implements **243 registered commands**. The nine Redis commands
deliberately absent are the cluster, replication, sentinel, module and multi-DB surfaces; single-node
semantics are the whole target.

It is a research system. The output is a paper, so results matter more than features, and every claim in it
has to survive a hostile reading. Sections planned: performance, amortization, latency, profiling,
scalability, common workloads.

## Architecture

**Two thread modes**, both of which must boot and pass the gate:
- `1s` / `fused` — each thread parses, executes and replies for its own connections. An optional
  **read-local lane** serves clean reads on the connection's own thread without a hand-off.
- `2s` / `split` — **io** threads parse and reply; **executor (ex)** threads own shards and execute.
  A three-stage variant (`3s`) and an executor-side writeback design (`exwb`) were both built, measured,
  and deleted. Do not propose either.

**Sharding and ownership.** Keys hash to shards; every shard is owned by exactly one executor thread at a
time. Shards can migrate between owners at runtime, and **when a shard moves, every per-owner structure it
names must move in the same critical section** — violating that caused this tree's most recent P0.

**Ordering ring (`rob`).** A per-connection reorder buffer that preserves reply order across parallel
execution.

**Atomics.** Multi-key atomicity uses group-scoped epoch-MVCC. Cross-shard commands use scatter-gather.
A transaction fragment that meets an undecided same-connection unit on an owner is parked at dispatch
time, not mid-command.

**Flip.** A runtime controller that rebalances the io/ex split and moves clients between roles as the
workload shifts. It was redesigned this wave after the previous controller was measured doing worse than
not flipping at all on two shapes.

**Load balancing.** Key-affine and client-affine balancing (`--key-lb`, `--client-lb`), both default on.

Networking is io_uring; the allocator is jemalloc.

## Non-negotiable correctness laws

Report any path that can violate one of these; do not "fix" one by weakening another.
- Single-owner writes.
- Reads are never obstructed by writes: immutable replacement plus QSBR. **No reader retries and no
  seqlocks on the per-operation path.**
- In-place overwrite is banned while the read-local lane is armed.
- Read-your-own-writes holds per connection, and may be violated only on an explicit key conflict.
- Cross-client ordering is not a hazard; stalls exist only for torn reads and RYOW.
- Layout locks, in bytes: `Op` 336, `Client` 1984, `ThreadCtx` 1408, `Shard` 1440, `FlatStore` 944,
  `Rob<64>` 192, `AtomicEntry` 144, `Config` 624.
- Both thread modes boot. Main commands carry zero regression. One file per feature.

## The box

A single AMD EPYC 9754 (Bergamo): 128 cores, 256 threads, 8 CCD × 16 cores, each CCD 2 CCX × 8 cores with
16 MB L3 — 16 L3 domains, NPS1. Measured node optimum is 8 cores, one CCX. Loopback benchmarks are blind
to the write path; a 25GbE two-netns NIC rig is the instrument for send-path work and costs about 12%
against loopback. Box noise is ±0.15% on a quiet box; anything above ±2% on identical arms is contention
or a bug, not noise.

**The gate boots nothing like a default server.** `tests/gate.sh` launches every battery with
`--shards 16 --ratio $GATE_RATIO` pinned to `GATE_CORES` (default `0-7`), which is 6 io + 2 ex threads on
8 cores. Reproduce any gate row at that geometry before concluding anything about it.

## What it is measured against

Redis 7.4 and 8.8.1, Dragonfly 1.40.2, KeyDB, Microsoft Garnet (net10.0), memcached 1.6.45, plus YCSB
0.17.0 traces. Binaries and digests: `/home/user/Projects/bench-bins/MANIFEST.md`.

We do not win everywhere and the paper will not claim we do. At 64 real cores and pipeline depth 128,
Garnet reaches 62.8M ops/s against our 34.4M. We hold depth 1, where we reach 4.35M. Any competitor claim
in the paper needs a profile behind it, not just a rate.

## How performance is judged

**cycles/op = instructions/op ÷ IPC.** Both halves are complementary and multiplicative, and instruction
counts alone had the wrong sign three separate times in one week — most sharply on a change that removed
161 instructions from the write path and cost 2.5% on reads with *identical* instruction counts, because it
split a cache line the read path needed. Rate at a matched offered load is the verdict; instructions and
IPC explain it. Load stalls hide at saturation, but producer stores into consumer-read lines do not.

Every optimization lands with a PRE vs POST table. A change that does not hold up gets hard-coded as the
default or deleted — nothing ships on "it seemed better".

## Why this work looks the way it does

Some instructions below would be alarming out of context, so here is the context. This is a single-user
research box. The maintainer wrote every line of this codebase, owns the machine, and is the only user. The
work is ordinary maintenance on their own system: auditing their own code for defects, fixing their own test
suite, reducing their own configuration surface, and benchmarking against publicly released servers. Nothing
here touches anyone else's data, systems or accounts.

Four specifics that read oddly without the reason:

1. **"Never run the server, the benchmark or the gate."** This is about measurement integrity and nothing
   else. Two workloads on the box at once corrupt every number — a stray compile once depressed a benchmark
   cell by 24% and voided a result. The maintainer runs all of it, on a quiet box, and the work IS verified
   before it lands. You are being asked to produce a diff, not to skip verification.

2. **"Never edit `EXPECT_QUICK` / `EXPECT_FULL`."** Those constants are how many test rows must pass. Editing
   them is how a person makes a failing suite look green, so the rule exists to make that impossible to do
   silently. It is a stricter standard than normal, not a looser one. State what the count should become and
   why; the maintainer changes it.

3. **Concurrency vocabulary.** This is a database. "Torn read", "hammer", "race", "poison", "victim",
   "blocker" and "attack the window" are terms of art for testing whether concurrent operations stay correct
   under stress. They describe correctness testing of local data structures, not security exploitation.

4. **Deliberately breaking a mechanism to check a test.** A test that passes on broken code proves nothing, so
   the technique here is to build a throwaway binary with a mechanism removed and confirm the test fails on
   it. That build is never committed and never runs outside the box. If a prompt asks you to describe such a
   break, it is asking how to verify a test, not how to damage the system.

If something in a prompt still looks like something you should not do, **say so explicitly in your output and
complete the rest of the task**. A stated objection is useful. Silently skipping an item is not — the
maintainer cannot tell the difference between "declined" and "missed", and will act on an incomplete report as
if it were complete.

## Working rules for codex

- **Never run a server, a benchmark, or the gate.** The maintainer runs the box. Report, or produce a diff.
- Edit only inside your own worktree.
- Never edit `EXPECT_QUICK` / `EXPECT_FULL` in `tests/gate.sh`. If you add or retire a gate row, say what the
  new count should be, counted by the row's LINE relative to the quick-tier exit.
- Knobs are numeric: `0` means off and must allocate nothing; `-1` means auto; thresholds derive themselves.
  Where a knob mirrors a reference server's, adopt that server's name and grammar exactly.
- A test that cannot fail proves nothing. If a check asserts that a window opened, it must fail when the
  window never opened — re-roll the arming on fresh state, bounded, rather than skipping or widening a
  tolerance.

## Closed doors — measured, negative, do not re-propose

`3s` three-stage mode; `exwb` executor-side writeback (−11 to −22%); AMAC and any CR/MR split (the only
boundary is io/ex); reorder-and-window; seqlocks on the per-op path; connection-side record allocation
(`connalloc`, cycles flat, record born on the wrong core); executor-major task collapse (`exmajor`,
−2 to −3%); the read-local capacity hand-off line split (`t-pubdiet`, +1.97% SET but −2.50% GET).

1. **S storage 13 — MISPRICED: deadline-sidecar expiry.**  
   The ordinary build reads the object’s inline deadline. The stale-index deadline becomes authoritative only with `TOMO_TTL_DEADLINE_SIDECAR=1`, whose default is zero. The prototype failure remains credible: extend a deadline while the index needs allocation, fail that allocation, then read after the previous deadline. Classify this as a prototype-build defect requiring allocation failure. [Selector](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/store_ttl.h:8), [deadline accessor](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:1454).

2. **C concurrency 2 — MISPRICED: scheduler stack bounds.**  
   The stated `--overlap` and `--ex-sched` flags are rejected. However, their accepted replacements, `--x-overlap 1 --x-ex-sched 1`, still expose the mismatch in fused mode. A gathered batch containing at least 33 eligible commands reaches the 32-entry array before the single-client shortcut. This is a real memory-safety defect in an explicitly enabled experimental combination; it does not describe the default scheduler configuration. [Parser](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:632), [scheduler](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:2303).

3. **S cmdsem F08 — MISPRICED: failed/no-op writes dirty WATCH.**  
   The unconditional write-completion hook does dirty the declared key after `WRONGTYPE` or an unsuccessful `SET NX`. The supplied sequence therefore produces a spurious EXEC abort. The traced failure is pessimistic conflict detection: it does not admit a transaction that should fail or commit an incorrect value. Retain a compatibility/progress finding at reduced severity. [Completion hook](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:2967), [dirtying](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/multi.inc:2413).

Nevertheless, capture still reads plain counters concurrently, and an atomic load does not make a concurrent plain store race-free. Retain the C++ race and measurement-validity defect; keyspace corruption or process failure is not established by this claim. [Counter reads](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:1584), [RESETSTAT](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:2940), [LB reader](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/lbsignals.cc:14).

22. **C storage 3 — SURVIVES, with corrected consequence: atomic rehash capacity.**  
    A concrete source-derived geometry defeats the claimed drain-before-fill invariant. Start with capacity 1,024, 600 live entries occupying slots 424–1,023, and 100 tombstones. With atomic MSET, no expiry/AOF/new-key notification probes, and fresh 100-key owner groups, the first preflight starts a same-size rehash. After seven installs, `(rehash_pos, live0, live1)=(624,900,400)`. The eighth preflight moves 104 slots, reaching `(728,1004,296)`, then refuses its 100 new keys. Those moves persist. Further eight-slot advances exhaust table 0 while live old entries remain.  
    The 70% check is bypassed while rehashing, and MSET’s install loop supplies no compensating per-key rehash. Ordinary rehash now aborts on failed insertion; read-local rehash still discards the old slot without checking insertion success. Thus “silent loss” needs the read-local path; the ordinary path has a process-abort consequence. 29. **S atomics 16; S storage 4 — SURVIVES: rollback capacity.**  
    The speculative geometry can be made concrete. Start with 700 live keys in a 1,024-slot table. A cross-owner atomic DEL removing those 700 keys preflights a 2,048-slot destination. Delay its other fragment before failure. After local deletion, insert 1,400 unrelated keys, choosing them to reuse tombstones before empty slots; this remains below the ordinary 70% growth threshold. Now fail the delayed fragment and let cleanup allocations succeed. Restoring 700 distinct predecessors requires 2,100 live slots in capacity 2,048.

    Let A retain version V during its current pass, publish V+1, and let B refresh V+1. Move an A shard before A’s next refresh. Transfer neither configures the shard nor invalidates B’s cached version; B subsequently sees “unchanged” and skips it. With V disabling maxmemory and V+1 enabling it, the incoming store remains unbounded until another configuration publication. [Refresh](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:1885), [transfer](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/server.h:2080).

44. **S concurrency 8 — SURVIVES: stale notification-hint pointer.**  
    Key-LB publishes the new owner before the destination’s tail rebind. A lazy-expiring GET in its first resumed task drain can therefore write the former executor’s plain pending flag while that executor reads/clears it. The later forced drain and idle sweep address eventual service, not this race. FLIP’s install-time rebinding does protect its corresponding path; the surviving trigger is key-LB. [Transfer](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/server.h:2098), [deferred rebind](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:1858), [hint write](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/shard.h:167).

45. **S deadconf F02 — SURVIVES: rewrite drops accepted configuration.**  
    CONFIG REWRITE reconstructs the file exclusively from `g_config`. That table omits accepted inline `user` definitions and `load`, among other boot settings. Boot with inline ACLs and a nondefault recovery file, rewrite, then restart using that file without CLI overrides: those settings are absent. The comment permitting removal of unknown directives cannot justify dropping directives this parser accepts. [Emitted table](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:305), [writer](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/server_tail.cc:654), [accepted ACL grammar](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:545).

46. **S deadconf F03 — SURVIVES: rewrite fails string round-trip.**  
    Boot from a config containing a quoted password with spaces, then rewrite it. Nonempty strings are emitted without quoting or escaping, so the password becomes multiple tokens on restart. Newlines and quotes supply additional failure cases. Empty-string quoting is a special case and does not cover nonempty values. [Emission](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/server_tail.cc:681).

47. **S deadconf F04 — SURVIVES: concurrent rewrite inode collision.**  
    Two IO-local rewrites can open the same temporary file before either finishes. Let A write and rename it while B retains the same inode open; B can then overwrite the installed configuration, potentially leaving A’s trailing bytes if B’s snapshot is shorter. B’s eventual rename failure does not undo that write. The config mutex protects only snapshot collection. [File operations](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/server_tail.cc:690), [mutex lifetime](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:2933).

48. **S deadconf F05 — SURVIVES: boot password NUL truncation.**  
    A quoted `requirepass "secret\x00suffix"` creates an embedded NUL in the loader’s string. Passing it through C-string views and `strlen` authenticates against `secret`; a leading NUL disables the password. I checked the hex decoder and subsequent password publication. Protected mode may restrict connection origins, but it does not restore the specified password. [Decoder](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:1070), [password publication](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:412).

49. **S deadconf F06 — SURVIVES: missing requirepass value clears it.**  
    End accepted arguments with `--requirepass`, or use `--requirepass secret --requirepass`. The generic `next("")` fallback supplies an empty password instead of a parse error. There is no requirepass-specific missing-value validation afterward. Explicitly supplying an empty password is valid; silently substituting it for an omitted argument is the defect. [Argument helper](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:446), [password parser](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:543).

    Run `local ok=pcall(function() while true do end end); return 42`. The count hook raises an ordinary catchable Lua error. Removing dangerous globals does not remove base-library pcall. The fallback may preserve returned-value correctness; it still violates the explicit no-reader-retries contract.     On an established userspace TLS connection, pipeline `CLIENT REPLY SKIP; PING; PING`. Fully engaged kTLS encrypts ordinary socket writes and therefore does not demonstrate this particular failure. [Early exit](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:4108), [marking gate](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:4560), [completion helper](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:5375).

Those inspection completion cases never append the deferred bytes before erasing pending state. Modify/Reset handling does preserve them, but does not cover these cases. 55. **S netproto 6 — SURVIVES: marked operation swallows embedded pushes.**

The marking gate runs before pub/sub dispatch, so this is reachable.     A queue merely totaling over 4 GiB is not sufficient: the single-buffer overload splits large lengths correctly. The two-piece overload does not. Construct a list whose LRANGE reply exceeds 4 GiB, using individually admissible elements, and retire it while an earlier borrowed reply keeps segment mode active. The combined direct/spill length is narrowed into one `uint32_t` segment. LRANGE and SmallBuf impose no corresponding aggregate bound. 63. **S storage 5 — SURVIVES: overwrite re-enables snapshot eviction.**  
    During capture, first admit enough other growth to leave a shard over its normal budget. 64. **S storage 6 — SURVIVES: mixed atomic/plain flags access.**  
    Enable fused read-local with positive maxmemory and LFU/LRU touching. The foreign CAS covers the whole byte; plain owner loads remain conflicting accesses to that memory location. [Foreign update](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:1128), [mixed accessors](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/kvobj.h:162).

65. **S storage 7 — SURVIVES: atomic eviction absent from AOF.**  
    Persist an unrelated victim key, then force an atomic write’s admission to evict it under an allkeys policy. `atomic_admit` erases without the `record_delete` used by ordinary eviction. Group post-images cover command keys, not this unrelated victim. Before a replacing snapshot/rewrite, replaying that AOF with eviction disabled resurrects the victim. 66. **S storage 8 — SURVIVES: ordinary eviction ignores script intents.**  
    Pin and stage a key for a cross-owner script while it has no atomic record. Have an unrelated ordinary write evict that key. Victim selection excludes `atomic_has_record`, whereas the stronger intent-aware exclusion exists only in atomic admission. Script validation searches version records and therefore need not detect this unversioned eviction. The script’s staged view can subsequently commit despite the missing reserved predecessor. [Victim exclusion](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:2341), [validation](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:166).

67. **S storage 9 — SURVIVES: imported hash deadlines remain unregistered.**  
    Atomically COPY or cross-owner RENAME a hash carrying field TTLs onto a destination shard that has never registered any field expiry. Image loading preserves the TTL data, but atomic APPLY installs the object without `note_loaded_object`/`note_field_ttl`. CXX      ?= g++
JEDIR    ?= /home/user/Projects/refs/jemalloc/_install
# jemalloc is optional: without it the tree still builds and runs, using the deterministic portable
# size-class table in alloc.h. Set JE=0 to force that path (useful for A/B-ing the allocator).
JE       ?= 1
ifeq ($(JE),1)
  # Prefer the system package; fall back to the copy built from refs/.
  ifneq ($(wildcard /usr/include/jemalloc/jemalloc.h),)
    JEFLAGS := -DTOMO_JEMALLOC
    JELIBS  := -ljemalloc
  else
    JEFLAGS := -DTOMO_JEMALLOC -I$(JEDIR)/include
    JELIBS  := $(JEDIR)/lib/libjemalloc.a -ldl
  endif
else
  JEFLAGS :=
  JELIBS  :=
endif

build/src/cmd/t_string.o: CXXFLAGS += --param large-unit-insns=10600

# The armed-write block cache's ownership laws as assertions: the cache and the QSBR retire ring
# are owner-private (one thread, no lock), each cached block is resident exactly once, each class
# list matches its counter, and every shard's retire sink names its CURRENT owner. Debug-only: the
# residency set and the sampled list walk cost far more than the path they guard. DESIGN-P0REPLY.md.

	  -o build/tomokv-rlcachedbg $(JELIBS) $(LDLIBS) -lm

#!/bin/bash
# PRE-PUSH GATE for tomokv-cpp (pure 2s baseline).
#
#   tests/gate.sh quick   loopback only: build (release+ASAN), footprint locks, boot
#                         matrix, smoke, torture, RYOW, atomic torn/mixed-write/window gates,
#                         shutdown invariants, counter-fired assertions, idle-loop ceiling. Runs on
#                         any machine.
#   tests/gate.sh full    quick + torture-under-ASAN + the Redis 7.4 differential matrix + NIC
#                         regression cells vs tests/gate_refs.txt (the NIC cells need the 25GbE
#                         netns rig and its scratchpad binaries/procsafe helper).
#
#   Every feature battery runs on three boots: split (both atomic modes), fused, and fused with the
#   read-local lane ARMED (--read-local 1, the recommended read-heavy production posture; that leg
#   is the only one on which a clean GET/MGET is served by the lane instead of an owner).
#
#   GATE_QUIET_FILE=<path> (opt-in, for a shared box): nothing that starts CPU work -- a battery, a
#   boot, a build, a load generator -- is launched unless that file exists and is older than
#   GATE_QUIET_MINUTES (3). A running battery always finishes; a build is SIGSTOPped; the idle server
#   is SIGSTOPped while waiting; waited time is taken out of the ledger's per-row seconds and logged
#   to $LEDGER.pauses. GATE_LEDGER overrides the ledger path.
#
# The vacuous-validation rule is load-bearing here: every section proves its mechanism FIRED
# (counters, accepts, direct>0), not merely that nothing crashed. A gate that can pass while
# testing nothing is worse than no gate.
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
TIER=${1:-quick}
PORT=${GATE_PORT:-7899}
CORES=${GATE_CORES:-0-7}
NCORES=$(taskset -c "$CORES" nproc)
if [ "$NCORES" -ge 8 ]; then GATE_RATIO=6:$((NCORES-6))
else GATE_RATIO=$(((NCORES+1)/2)):$((NCORES-(NCORES+1)/2)); fi
PASS=0; FAIL=0
SRV=0; SRVLOG=/dev/null
GLOBCASE_ORACLE=0; MMPID=0
# The pinned vanilla Redis 7.4 tree (source + built src/redis-server). The ACL-category generator
# reads its SOURCE in both tiers; the differential and globcase rows boot its BINARY in the full
# tier. The preflight below says exactly what is missing instead of a traceback in row 4.
export REDIS74_ROOT=${REDIS74_ROOT:-/tmp/claude-1000/redis74}
# Wall-time bound per battery (see py()). A hung battery used to hang the whole gate; now it is a
# red row that says TIMEOUT. 900 s is ~3x the slowest battery on the gate cores. flipctl.py is
# launched with its own explicit 600 s bound (it re-rolls a non-stationary stable hold; see there).
GATE_TEST_TIMEOUT=${GATE_TEST_TIMEOUT:-900}
# A battery that records a STRICT skip (a DEBUG hook it needed was denied) fails under the gate:
# a gate row must run the arm it exists for, never turn green by skipping it (tests/_lib.py).
export TOMO_GATE_STRICT=1
# Machine-readable ledger, one line per row: verdict, seconds since the previous row, label.
# It is the runtime-distribution instrument (which rows own the 45 minutes) and, when the count
# drifts, the diff against the previous run's ledger names the row that vanished or appeared.
LEDGER=${GATE_LEDGER:-/tmp/gate-ledger-$TIER.txt}
[ -f "$LEDGER" ] && mv -f "$LEDGER" "$LEDGER.prev"
: > "$LEDGER"
ROW_T=$(date +%s.%N)
# Expected check counts. These are the whole point of the ledger row: a battery that silently
# stops running drops the count and turns the gate red instead of quietly shrinking coverage.
# Bump them DELIBERATELY when rows are added, and say which rows in the commit message.
# 152 -> 172: the s6 oracle battery, concur, execiso and xacct, each under both atomic modes.
# 172 -> 178: snapcut added two cross-shard snapshot-cut rows per persist-io engine, and execfix
# added its battery under both atomic modes.
# 178 -> 184: edgeproto, edgeenc and edgetime batteries joined the feature loop (both modes each).
# 184 -> 189: cross-owner scripts add their battery under both atomic modes plus three control
# boots (off / byte-limit / window), each needing its own knob value and so its own server.
# 189 -> 192: the three efficiency guards, each on its own boot geometry.
# 192 -> 194: the AOF frame-order battery, on persist-io normal under both atomic modes.
# 194 -> 207: arity, blockmulti, cmdgap, multires and xmove were shipped but not invoked; aclsel,
# cmdmeta and expwide joined the feature loop; cmdmeta coverage is a new static row. Each feature

say(){ printf '  %-52s %s\n' "$1" "$2"; }
ledger(){ # verdict label -> one ledger line; the elapsed column is wall time since the last row
  local now; now=$(date +%s.%N)
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$(awk -v a="$ROW_T" -v b="$now" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", b-a}')" "$2" \
      >> "$LEDGER"
  ROW_T=$now
}
ok(){ say "$1" "ok"; PASS=$((PASS+1)); ledger ok "$1"; }
bad(){ say "$1" "FAIL${2:+ ($2)}"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); ledger FAIL "$1"; }
ledger_labels(){ cut -f3 "$1" | sed 's/[0-9][0-9]*/N/g' | sort; }
program_state(){
  local expect=$1 actual=$((PASS+FAIL))
  if [ "$actual" -eq "$expect" ]; then
    say "PROGRAM-STATE ledger ($actual/$expect checks)" "ok"
  else
    bad "PROGRAM-STATE ledger" "$actual/$expect checks"
    if [ -f "$LEDGER.prev" ]; then
      echo "  rows that differ from the previous $TIER ledger (< only in previous run, > only now):"
      diff <(ledger_labels "$LEDGER.prev") <(ledger_labels "$LEDGER") | grep '^[<>]' | sed 's/^/    /'
    fi
  fi
  echo "  ledger: $LEDGER (verdict / seconds since previous row / label); slowest rows:"
  sort -t "$(printf '\t')" -k2,2 -rn "$LEDGER" | head -12 \
      | awk -F '\t' '{printf "    %7.1fs  %-4s %s\n", $2, $1, $3}'
}
redis_cli_expect_ok(){
  local reply
  reply=$(redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 -p "$PORT" "$@" 2>&1 | tr -d '\r')
  [ "$reply" = OK ] || { printf 'unexpected redis-cli reply to %s: %s\n' "$*" "$reply" >&2; return 1; }
}
# Cooperative box sharing (opt-in, see header). quiet_ok is the whole rule; its two callers are
# quiet_wait (before anything that starts CPU work) and pausable (around a build -- the one kind
# of row long enough to need stopping mid-flight and free of timing semantics).
QUIET_FILE=${GATE_QUIET_FILE:-}
QUIET_MIN=${GATE_QUIET_MINUTES:-3}
PAUSABLE_PID=0
quiet_ok(){ [ -z "$QUIET_FILE" ] || [ -n "$(find "$QUIET_FILE" -mmin +"$QUIET_MIN" 2>/dev/null)" ]; }
quiet_note(){ printf '%s %s\n' "$(date '+%H:%M:%S')" "$*" | tee -a "$LEDGER.pauses" >&2; }
quiet_wait(){ # block until quiet_ok. The live server is SIGSTOPped meanwhile (an idle fused loop
              # still spins on cores an owner measurement may share); the waited time leaves the
              # ledger's next row, which measures rows, not the box.
  quiet_ok && return 0
  local t0 now stopped=0
  t0=$(date +%s.%N)
  if [ "$SRV" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && kill -0 "$SRV" 2>/dev/null; then
    kill -STOP "$SRV" 2>/dev/null && stopped=1
  fi
  quiet_note "quiet: waiting for $QUIET_FILE to be >$QUIET_MIN min old" \
      "($([ "$stopped" = 1 ] && echo "server $SRV stopped" || echo "no server up"))"
  until quiet_ok; do sleep 5; done
  [ "$stopped" = 1 ] && kill -CONT "$SRV" 2>/dev/null
  now=$(date +%s.%N)
  ROW_T=$(awk -v a="$ROW_T" -v b="$t0" -v c="$now" 'BEGIN{printf "%.9f", a + (c - b)}')
  quiet_note "quiet: resumed after $(awk -v b="$t0" -v c="$now" 'BEGIN{printf "%.0f", c - b}')s"
}
pausable(){ # run "$@" to completion (its exit status is ours); SIGSTOP its whole process group
            # whenever quiet_ok turns false and SIGCONT it when the file is back. Builds only.
  [ -n "$QUIET_FILE" ] || { "$@"; return $?; }
  quiet_wait
  local pid stopped=0 t0=0 paused=0 rc
  setsid "$@" &
  pid=$!; PAUSABLE_PID=$pid
  while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
    if quiet_ok; then
      if [ "$stopped" = 1 ]; then
        kill -CONT -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null; stopped=0
        paused=$(awk -v p="$paused" -v b="$t0" -v c="$(date +%s.%N)" \
                     'BEGIN{printf "%.3f", p + (c - b)}')
        quiet_note "quiet: build resumed"
      fi
    elif [ "$stopped" = 0 ]; then
      kill -STOP -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null; stopped=1; t0=$(date +%s.%N)
      quiet_note "quiet: build paused until $QUIET_FILE is >$QUIET_MIN min old"
    fi
    sleep 2
  done
  wait "$pid"; rc=$?
  PAUSABLE_PID=0
  ROW_T=$(awk -v a="$ROW_T" -v p="$paused" 'BEGIN{printf "%.9f", a + p}')
  return $rc
}
py(){ # python3 battery wrapper: bounded wall time. A timeout or a self-skip (exit 3, see
      # tests/_lib.skip_all) is named in the row's log (callers redirect our stderr there) and
      # stays RED: a row that cannot run is a gate defect, not a pass. --foreground keeps the
      # battery in the terminal's process group so Ctrl-C reaches it too.
  local rc
  quiet_wait
  timeout --foreground "$GATE_TEST_TIMEOUT" python3 "$@"; rc=$?
  case $rc in
    124) echo "GATE: TIMEOUT -- battery killed after ${GATE_TEST_TIMEOUT}s" >&2;;
    3)   echo "GATE: battery SKIPPED ITSELF (exit 3): a gate row must run, not skip" >&2;;
  esac
  return $rc
}
cleanup(){ # EXIT/INT/TERM: never leave the server on $PORT, the globcase oracle, or memtier behind
  local p
  if [ "$PAUSABLE_PID" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then   # a build parked by pausable
    kill -CONT -- "-$PAUSABLE_PID" 2>/dev/null; kill -TERM -- "-$PAUSABLE_PID" 2>/dev/null

// kvobj.h — one key-value pair in ONE allocation.
//
// Layout, contiguous, in this order:
//
//   [ hdr 8B ][ klen_ext u32? ][ expire_at i64? ][ key bytes ][ value: bytes | ptr | i64 | compact ]
//
// Three rules drive this, all of them measured on the fork rather than assumed:
//
//  1. ALLOCATION COUNT is the lever (a bespoke size-class pool was built and deleted; the measured
//     win was fewer allocations, not cleverer ones). So key and value live in the same block as the
//     header, and small values never allocate separately. Embedding was worth +27% on SET.
//  2. NO REFCOUNT. Redis's robj refcount is a cross-thread hazard in a sharded server and its
//     traffic is a shared-line write. A KvObj is owned outright by one shard: copy or move, never
//     share. There is no shared-integer cache either.
//  3. NOTHING STORED THAT THE TABLE ALREADY HAS. FlatStore's slot carries a 15-bit tag, so no hash
//     is kept here. Optional LRU/LFU state steals proven-spare header bits; it adds no field.
//
// BUDGET (an aspiration with no test behind it yet; there is no bench/kvobj_footprint in the tree):
//   16-byte key + 64-byte value, no TTL  ->  target < 85 B all-in.

#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <memory>
#include <new>

#include "../base/alloc.h"
#include "../net/resp.h"
#include "read_local_settax.h"
#include "store_ttl.h"
#include "typeval.h"

namespace tomo {

enum class Type : uint8_t {
    String = 0, Hash = 1, List = 2, Set = 3, Zset = 4, Stream = 5,
};

enum class Enc : uint8_t {
    Raw    = 0,   // value bytes inline in this block
    Int    = 1,   // value IS an int64 held in the block; no bytes, no allocation
    Extern = 2,   // value lives in a separate block; the slot holds a void*
    Compact = 3,  // collection metadata and packed bytes live in the KvObj tail
};

inline constexpr uint32_t kEmbedThreshold = 192;

static_assert(static_cast<uint8_t>(Type::Stream) < (1u << 3),
              "selector 3 reserves three header bits for Type");
static_assert(static_cast<uint8_t>(Enc::Compact) < (1u << 2),
              "selector 3 reserves two header bits for Enc");

struct KvObjFlags {
    // Physical layout bit: an eight-byte deadline slot follows klen_ext.  PERSIST writes -1 into
    // that slot; logical volatility is KvObj::has_ttl(), not this bit alone.
    static constexpr uint8_t HasTtl = 1u << 0;
    static constexpr uint8_t KeyExt = 1u << 1;   // klen did not fit in 8 bits; u32 follows the hdr
    // Re-headering a collection moves this ownership bit to the replacement before FlatStore
    // retires the old header. Both headers briefly name the pointer; exactly one may destroy it.
    static constexpr uint8_t OwnsExtern = 1u << 2;
    // Bits 3..7 are the optional five-bit eviction metadata. They are never written while
    // maxmemory is disabled. See KvObj::eviction_meta().
    static constexpr uint8_t LayoutMask = HasTtl | KeyExt | OwnsExtern;
};

// Header is exactly 8 bytes. Selector 3 spends the otherwise redundant high bits of Type/Enc to
// co-locate both in byte zero, freeing the old encoding byte for Raw's bounded (<=192) length. The
// aligned word at offset four is then a full, non-wrapping object sequence for Raw; flags and key
// length retain their old offsets, and other encodings retain the original 32-bit vlen meaning.
// All other selectors preserve the complete original byte layout.
struct KvObj {
#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
    uint8_t  type : 3;  // Type needs 0..5
    uint8_t  enc : 2;   // Enc needs 0..3
    uint8_t  type_enc_spare : 3;
    uint8_t  raw_vlen;  // Enc::Raw only; all other encodings leave this zero
    uint8_t  flags;     // KvObjFlags
    uint8_t  klen8;     // key length when < 255; 255 means "see the u32 after the header"
    union {
        uint32_t vlen;         // non-Raw inline/external length
        uint32_t raw_sequence; // Enc::Raw odd/even publication sequence
    };
#else
    uint8_t  type;      // Type
    uint8_t  enc;       // Enc
    uint8_t  flags;     // KvObjFlags
    uint8_t  klen8;     // key length when < 255; 255 means "see the u32 after the header"
    uint32_t vlen;      // inline value length, or external length when Enc::Extern
#endif

    Enc encoding() const { return static_cast<Enc>(enc); }

        return vlen;
#endif

        raw_vlen = static_cast<uint8_t>(length);
        raw_sequence = 0;
#else
        vlen = length;
#endif
    }
    void init_nonraw_length(uint32_t length) {

        raw_vlen = 0;
#endif

        return 0;
#endif
    }

#else
        return 0;
#endif
    }

#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3

#else

#endif
    }
    void close_raw_sequence(uint32_t even) {
#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
        std::atomic_ref<uint32_t>(raw_sequence).store(even + 2u, std::memory_order_release);
#else
        (void)even;
#endif
    }

    void set_eviction_meta(uint8_t meta) {

    // Foreign fused readers use atomic flag loads because the owner may update the five eviction
    // bits in place. Layout bits remain immutable for a published read-local-eligible string.
    uint8_t read_local_flags() const { return __atomic_load_n(&flags, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE); }
    void set_eviction_meta_atomic(uint8_t meta) {

    uint32_t ttl_bytes()      const { return (flags & KvObjFlags::HasTtl) ? 8u : 0u; }

    char*       tail()       { return reinterpret_cast<char*>(this) + sizeof(KvObj); }
    const char* tail() const { return reinterpret_cast<const char*>(this) + sizeof(KvObj); }

    uint32_t klen() const {
        if (flags & KvObjFlags::KeyExt) {
            uint32_t k;
            std::memcpy(&k, tail(), 4);
            return k;
        }
        return klen8;

    char*       key_ptr()       { return tail() + klen_ext_bytes() + ttl_bytes(); }
    const char* key_ptr() const { return tail() + klen_ext_bytes() + ttl_bytes(); }

    uint32_t read_local_klen(uint8_t stable_flags) const {
        if (stable_flags & KvObjFlags::KeyExt) {

    }
    const char* read_local_key_ptr(uint8_t stable_flags) const {

        const uint32_t ttl = (stable_flags & KvObjFlags::HasTtl) ? 8u : 0u;

    char*       val_ptr()       { return key_ptr() + klen(); }
    const char* val_ptr() const { return key_ptr() + klen(); }

        int64_t t;
        std::memcpy(&t, tail() + klen_ext_bytes(), 8);
        return t;

    TtlState ttl_state() const { return TtlState{expire_at_ms(), has_ttl_slot()}; }
    int64_t read_local_expire_at_ms(uint8_t stable_flags) const {
        if (!(stable_flags & KvObjFlags::HasTtl)) return -1;

    Slice str_value() const {

// store_ttl.h -- retained deadline-slot state and the deadline-sidecar bake-off selector.
//
// The sidecar prototype deliberately does not change KvObj's layout contract: it selects the
// owner's deadline lookup source while the in-object slot remains the immutable-version fallback.
#pragma once
#include <cstdint>

#ifndef TOMO_TTL_DEADLINE_SIDECAR
#define TOMO_TTL_DEADLINE_SIDECAR 0
#endif

namespace tomo {

static_assert(TOMO_TTL_DEADLINE_SIDECAR == 0 || TOMO_TTL_DEADLINE_SIDECAR == 1,
              "TOMO_TTL_DEADLINE_SIDECAR must be 0 (inline) or 1 (sidecar prototype)");

inline constexpr bool kTtlDeadlineSidecar = TOMO_TTL_DEADLINE_SIDECAR == 1;
inline constexpr int64_t kNoTtlDeadline = -1;

// A deadline describes logical volatility; reserve_slot carries the allocation's physical
// history through TTL-preserving replacements. A plain value replacement may instead start with
// the default state and thereby begin a new lifetime without a reserved slot.
struct TtlState {
    int64_t deadline = kNoTtlDeadline;
    bool reserve_slot = false;

    constexpr bool has_deadline() const { return deadline >= 0; }
    constexpr bool needs_deadline_slot() const { return reserve_slot || has_deadline(); }

    // Test logical volatility first: a retained slot stores -1 and must never look expired.
    constexpr bool expired(int64_t now_ms) const {
        return has_deadline() && deadline <= now_ms;
    }

    // Arming a TTL creates a lifetime reservation. Replacing an existing deadline, or clearing it
    // with a negative sentinel, cannot discard a slot already present in this value lifetime.
    constexpr TtlState with_deadline(int64_t new_deadline) const {
        const bool armed = new_deadline >= 0;
        return {
            armed ? new_deadline : kNoTtlDeadline,
            needs_deadline_slot() || armed,
        };
    }

    constexpr TtlState persisted() const {
        return {kNoTtlDeadline, needs_deadline_slot()};
    }
};

}  // namespace tomo

// flatstore_atomic.inc — epoch-MVCC members textually included inside class FlatStore.
//
// This file is intentionally not a standalone header. Keeping these definitions inside the
// header-only class preserves the original single-TU concatenation model without new external
// symbols, translation units, or build-system changes.

    // Main calls this only after every IO/ex thread has joined. It releases group references before
    // IO-owned arena pools are destroyed; the destructor repeats it harmlessly for early exits.
    void atomic_shutdown_release_records() { atomic_promote_all_for_shutdown(); }

    // bindings are installed once at boot; the null tracker pointer below is the complete
    // disabled-feature tax on store accesses.
    // FLUSH's logical clear is the store's only ticket draw. It goes through the server's
    // reserve/publish bracket rather than touching commit_seq_ directly, so the visible read
    // watermark can never be left behind a ticket this store already installed.

                           uint64_t* predecessor_reads, uint64_t* chain_max,
                           uint64_t* promotions, uint64_t* records_freed,
                           uint64_t* entries, uint64_t* gauge_underflows) {
        atomic_ticket_fn_ = ticket_fn;
        atomic_ticket_ctx_ = ticket_ctx;
        atomic_activity_ = activity;
        atomic_script_intents_ = script_intents;
        atomic_predecessor_reads_ = predecessor_reads;
        atomic_chain_max_ = chain_max;
        atomic_promotions_ = promotions;
        atomic_records_freed_ = records_freed;
        atomic_entries_ = entries;
        atomic_gauge_underflows_ = gauge_underflows;
    }

    bool atomic_has_records() const {
        return atomic_pending_ &&

    }
    uint32_t atomic_pending_entries() const {
        return atomic_pending_ ? atomic_pending_->live : 0;
    }
    uint64_t atomic_cleanup_fast() const {
        return atomic_pending_ ? atomic_pending_->cleanup_fast : 0;
    }
    uint64_t atomic_cleanup_slow() const {
        return atomic_pending_ ? atomic_pending_->cleanup_slow : 0;
    }

        return atomic_key_pending(hash, key);

             intent = intent->next) {

                entry->group_aborted->load(std::memory_order_acquire)) continue;
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < entry->count; i++) {
                if (atomic_entry_hash(*entry, i) != hash ||
                    !atomic_entry_key(*entry, i).key_eq(key)) continue;
                const uint64_t epoch = atomic_epoch(*entry);
                if (!epoch || epoch > cut) return true;
            }
        }
        return false;
    }
    // Same-connection program order is the only ordering dependency between pipelined commands.
    // Foreign undecided nodes never block: resolution simply skips them.
    // A caller that has to exclude its OWN logical unit cannot do it here: a transaction spreads
    // over several epoch words (its own plus one per lowered cross-shard child) and one
    // `ignore_group` pointer names none of them. That question has its own probe --
    // atomic_has_foreign_unit_undecided(), below, which takes the predicate.
    bool atomic_has_own_undecided(uint64_t hash, Slice key, uint64_t origin_conn_id,
                                  const ScatterState* ignore_group = nullptr) const {
        if (!atomic_pending_) return false;
        const uint64_t bit = atomic_membership_bit(hash);
        const uint32_t bucket = static_cast<uint32_t>(mix64(origin_conn_id)) & 63;
        for (AtomicEntry* entry = atomic_pending_->conn_heads[bucket]; entry;
             entry = entry->conn_next) {
            if (!(entry->membership & bit) || !entry->group_epoch ||
                entry->origin_conn_id != origin_conn_id || entry->group == ignore_group)
                continue;
            if (entry->group_epoch->load(std::memory_order_acquire) != 0) continue;
            if (entry->group_aborted && entry->group_aborted->load(std::memory_order_acquire))
                continue;
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < entry->count; i++)
                if (atomic_entry_hash(*entry, i) == hash &&
                    atomic_entry_key(*entry, i).key_eq(key)) return true;
        }
        return false;
    }
    template <typename KeyAt>
    bool atomic_group_has_own_undecided(const ScatterState* group, uint32_t count,
                                        uint64_t origin_conn_id, uint64_t membership,
                                        KeyAt&& key_at) const {
        if (!atomic_pending_ || !group || !count) return false;
        if (!membership)
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++)
                membership |= atomic_membership_bit(key_at(i).first);
        const uint32_t bucket = static_cast<uint32_t>(mix64(origin_conn_id)) & 63;
        for (AtomicEntry* entry = atomic_pending_->conn_heads[bucket]; entry;
             entry = entry->conn_next) {
            if (!entry->group_epoch || entry->origin_conn_id != origin_conn_id ||
                entry->group == group || !(entry->membership & membership)) continue;
            if (entry->group_epoch->load(std::memory_order_acquire) != 0) continue;
            if (entry->group_aborted && entry->group_aborted->load(std::memory_order_acquire))
                continue;
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
                const auto [hash, key] = key_at(i);
                if (!(entry->membership & atomic_membership_bit(hash))) continue;
                for (uint32_t j = 0; j < entry->count; j++)
                    if (atomic_entry_hash(*entry, j) == hash &&
                        atomic_entry_key(*entry, j).key_eq(key)) return true;
            }
        }
        return false;
    }
    // Does this owner still hold an UNDECIDED record belonging to a DIFFERENT logical unit of
    // the same connection? A cross-shard atomic group installs its candidate physically before it
    // knows its own verdict -- MSETNX discovers an existing key on another owner, and any group
    // can still fail on OOM/maxmemory -- so such a record may yet be withdrawn. Program order
    // makes it this connection's business alone: foreign connections never see an epoch-zero
    // record at all, and a same-connection reader must not run past it.
    // `is_own` names the caller's OWN unit BY EPOCH WORD, and it must recognise every word that
    // unit publishes through, not just one: an EXEC's plain per-key installs use the transaction's
    // epoch, while each cross-shard child command lowered inside that EXEC keeps its own
    // ScatterState and therefore its own. Answering with only the transaction's word makes a
    // transaction hold against its own RENAME/LMPOP child and hang -- the same self-hold
    // NOTES-MULTIRES.md §5(a) hit from the other direction. Plain single-command pseudo-entries
    // carry no group_epoch at all: they draw their ticket in the same owner turn that installs
    // them, so they are never undecided and are skipped here.
    template <typename IsOwnUnit>
    bool atomic_has_foreign_unit_undecided(uint64_t origin_conn_id, IsOwnUnit&& is_own) const {
        if (!atomic_pending_ || !atomic_pending_->live) return false;
        const uint32_t bucket = static_cast<uint32_t>(mix64(origin_conn_id)) & 63;
            uint32_t* offsets = entry->group_key_offsets();
            const uint32_t begin = index ? offsets[index - 1] : 0;
            const uint64_t end = static_cast<uint64_t>(begin) + key.n;
            if (end > entry->key_len) std::abort();
            if (key.n) std::memcpy(entry->group_key_data() + begin, key.p, key.n);
            offsets[index] = static_cast<uint32_t>(end);
        }
        KvObj* old = atomic_exchange_physical(hash, key, value);
        entry->parked()[index] = old;
        entry->count = index + 1;
        return old;
    }

    void atomic_finish_group_install(size_t parked_bytes, size_t installed_bytes) {
        // atomic_admit charged every incoming object before its exchange. Once the whole shard pass
        // is physical, only the displaced predecessors remain version bytes. Fold the owner-local
        // gauge change into one write instead of mutating it twice for every installed key.
        atomic_version_bytes_ += parked_bytes;
        atomic_gauge_sub(installed_bytes);
    }

    // THE ONE PLACE THE VERSION-BYTES GAUGE SHRINKS.  It used to be `-=` at eleven sites plus one
    // std::abort() guard at the group-install site, which meant an over-decrement anywhere wrapped
    // the gauge and the process died in whichever unrelated group pass next noticed the wrap.  The
    // over-decrement it was catching was real (a read-modify-write mutated an already-parked
    // predecessor in place, so collapse returned more bytes than install had charged), but that is
    // a resolver defect, fixed in atomic_resolve_internal; killing the server over a memory
    // ACCOUNTING number is a strictly worse failure than carrying a mis-sized one.  Clamp, count,
    // and let a test assert the count is zero.  atomic_gauge_underflows is in INFO stats.
    void atomic_gauge_sub(size_t bytes) {
        if (__builtin_expect(bytes > atomic_version_bytes_, false)) {
            if (atomic_gauge_underflows_) (*atomic_gauge_underflows_)++;
            atomic_version_bytes_ = 0;
            return;
        }
        atomic_version_bytes_ -= bytes;
    }

    void atomic_publish_group(void* opaque) {
        auto* entry = static_cast<AtomicEntry*>(opaque);
        if (!entry || !entry->count || entry->linked) std::abort();
        atomic_link_entry(*entry);
    }


    // Guarantee room in table 0 for a whole owner install pass of `additional` keys, running the
    // SAME resize discipline as the ordinary insert() path so the atomic path shares its two hard
    // guarantees: (1) grow at kLoadPct (70%), not at 100% -- a table run to full has no free slot
    // and insert_into would fail; (2) reclaim tombstones. Every atomic detach leaves a tombstone,
    // and DELETE passes attach nothing, so without a reclaiming trigger on every pass (this is
    // called for deletes too, unlike the old value-writes-only reserve) tombstones fill the table.
    // Once it returns true, the group's physical install pass cannot hit a capacity
    // failure. Returns false only on real OOM (calloc) or a locked snapshot with no raw room.
    bool atomic_prepare_capacity(uint32_t additional) {
        if (__builtin_expect(read_local_enabled_, false))
            return atomic_prepare_capacity_read_local(additional);
        if (rehashing()) {
            if (!snapshot_active_) {
                // Keep drain ahead of fill: advance at least `additional` keys' worth of slots so
                // table 0 cannot fill before this rehash finishes (mirrors insert()'s 1-key : 8-slot
                // ratio, generalised to a whole install pass).
                uint32_t steps = additional / kRehashSlotsPerOp + 1;
                while (steps-- && rehashing()) rehash_step();
            }
            if (rehashing())
                return static_cast<uint64_t>(live_[0]) + tombs_[0] + additional < cap_[0];
            // fell through: rehash completed, re-evaluate against the merged table below.
        }
        if ((static_cast<uint64_t>(live_[0]) + tombs_[0] + additional) * 100 <
            static_cast<uint64_t>(cap_[0]) * kLoadPct)
            return true;
        if (snapshot_prepared_)
            return static_cast<uint64_t>(live_[0]) + tombs_[0] + additional < cap_[0];
        // Size for the LIVE set plus the pass (tombstones are dropped by the coming rehash). When
        // tombstones dominate and the live set is small this leaves `wanted == cap_[0]`: a same-size
        // rehash that reclaims them, exactly maybe_start_grow()'s policy.
        uint64_t wanted = cap_[0];
        const uint64_t need = static_cast<uint64_t>(live_[0]) + additional;
        while (need * 100 >= wanted * kLoadPct) {
            wanted *= uint64_t{2};
            if (wanted > UINT32_MAX) return false;
        }
        auto* fresh = static_cast<uint64_t*>(
            flatstore_table_calloc(static_cast<size_t>(wanted), sizeof(uint64_t)));
        if (!fresh) return false;
        tab_[1] = tab_[0]; cap_[1] = cap_[0]; mask_[1] = mask_[0];
        live_[1] = live_[0]; tombs_[1] = tombs_[0];
        tab_[0] = fresh; cap_[0] = static_cast<uint32_t>(wanted); mask_[0] = cap_[0] - 1;
        live_[0] = tombs_[0] = 0;
        rehash_pos_ = 0;
        return true;
    }

    bool atomic_admit(Slice protected_key, const KvObj* incoming) {
        const size_t bytes = incoming ? kvobj_size(incoming) : 0;
        if (!__builtin_expect(maxmemory_enabled_, false) || snapshot_active_) {
            atomic_version_bytes_ += bytes;
            return true;
        }
        auto fits = [&] {
            const size_t used = accounted_bytes();
            return bytes <= maxmemory_limit_ && used <= maxmemory_limit_ - bytes;
        };
        if (fits()) { atomic_version_bytes_ += bytes; return true; }
        if (maxmemory_policy_ == MaxmemoryPolicy::NoEviction) return false;
        uint32_t budget = kEvictionsPerOp;
        while (budget-- && !fits()) {
            KvObj* victim = choose_victim(protected_key);
            if (!victim) return false;
            const uint64_t hash = hash_key(victim->key());
            const Slice key = victim->key();
            // A key an in-flight group or a staged cross-owner script depends on is not a legal
            // victim: evicting it would destroy the predecessor those readers resolve against.
            if (atomic_needs_version(hash, key)) continue;
            const uint32_t before = size();
            const bool live = erase(hash, key);
            if (size() == before) return false;
            if (live && evicted_counter_) (*evicted_counter_)++;
        }
        if (!fits()) return false;
        atomic_version_bytes_ += bytes;
        return true;
    }

    void atomic_unadmit(const KvObj* incoming) {
        if (incoming) atomic_gauge_sub(kvobj_size(incoming));
    }

    void* atomic_acquire_value_block(size_t allocation) {
        allocation = good_size(allocation);
        if (!atomic_ensure_pending()) return nullptr;
        const uint32_t cls = atomic_pool_class(allocation);
        if (cls < AtomicPendingState::kPoolClasses && atomic_pending_->free_values[cls]) {
            auto* block = atomic_pending_->free_values[cls];
            if (block->allocation != allocation) std::abort();
            atomic_pending_->free_values[cls] = block->next;
            atomic_pending_->cached_value_bytes -= allocation;
#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
            std::destroy_at(block);
            return ::new (block) KvObj;
#else
            return block;
#endif
        }
#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
        void* memory = alloc_raw(allocation);
        return memory ? ::new (memory) KvObj : nullptr;
#else
        return alloc_raw(allocation);
#endif
    }

    void atomic_discard_value(KvObj* value) {
        if (!atomic_recycle_value(value)) kvobj_free(value);
    }

    bool atomic_prepare_plain(Slice key, uint64_t hash, uint64_t origin_conn_id,
                              void*& opaque) {
        if (__builtin_expect(read_local_enabled_, false))
            return atomic_prepare_plain_read_local(key, hash, origin_conn_id, opaque);
        opaque = nullptr;
                    first_tomb = slot;
                    have_first_tomb = true;
                }
                if (object && tag_of_word(word) == tag && object->key().key_eq(key)) {
                    obj_bytes_ -= kvobj_size(object);
                    if (replacement && table == 0) {
                        (void)track_expire(hash, replacement);
                        read_local_slot_store(&tab_[table][slot], make_word(tag, replacement));
                        obj_bytes_ += kvobj_size(replacement);
                    } else {
                        untrack_expire(hash);
                        read_local_slot_store(&tab_[table][slot], kTombBit);
                        live_[table]--; tombs_[table]++;
                    }
                    return object;
                }
                slot = (slot + 1) & mask_[table];
            }
            return nullptr;
        };
        auto insert_replacement = [&] {
            if (!replacement) return;
            if (!have_insertion_slot) std::abort();
            read_local_slot_store(
                &tab_[0][insertion_slot], make_word(tag_of(hash), replacement));
            if (insertion_reuses_tomb) tombs_[0]--;
            live_[0]++;
            const size_t added_bytes = kvobj_size(replacement);
            obj_bytes_ += added_bytes;
#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
            settax_stats().accounting_add_calls++;
            settax_stats().accounting_bytes += added_bytes;
#endif
            // The folded probe publishes without insert_into_read_local, so it owes the selected
            // tracker the same registration that path performs. Going through the flag alone would
            // register a PERSISTed key that merely RETAINS its slot, and would hand the sidecar
            // prototype an entry with no deadline payload.
            (void)track_expire(hash, replacement);
#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
            if (replacement->expire_at_ms() < 0) settax_stats().expire_erases++;
#endif
        };
        if (KvObj* object = exchange(0)) return object;
        if (rehashing()) {
            if (KvObj* object = exchange(1)) {
                insert_replacement();
                return object;
            }
        }
        insert_replacement();
        return nullptr;
    }

    // Swap a key in its existing slot, or retain the first tombstone and terminal empty while
    // proving it absent so a new replacement installs without repeating the current-table probe.
    // Atomic ownership needs the displaced pointer, so insert_into's ordinary retire-in-place path
    // is not usable.
    KvObj* atomic_exchange_physical(uint64_t hash, Slice key, KvObj* replacement) {
        if (__builtin_expect(read_local_enabled_, false))
            return atomic_exchange_physical_read_local(hash, key, replacement);
        uint32_t insertion_slot = 0;
        bool have_insertion_slot = false;
        bool insertion_reuses_tomb = false;
        auto exchange = [&](int table) -> KvObj* {
            if (!tab_[table]) return nullptr;
            const uint16_t tag = tag_of(hash);
            uint32_t slot = slot_start(table, hash);
            uint32_t first_tomb = 0;
            bool have_first_tomb = false;
            const bool retain_insertion = replacement && table == 0;
            for (uint32_t probes = 0; probes <= cap_[table]; probes++) {
                const uint64_t word = tab_[table][slot];
                if (word == 0) {
                    if (retain_insertion) {
                        insertion_slot = have_first_tomb ? first_tomb : slot;
                        insertion_reuses_tomb = have_first_tomb;
                        have_insertion_slot = true;
                    }
                    return nullptr;
                }
                KvObj* object = ptr_of(word);
                if (retain_insertion && !object && !have_first_tomb) {
                    first_tomb = slot;
                    have_first_tomb = true;
                }
                if (object && tag_of_word(word) == tag && object->key().key_eq(key)) {
                    obj_bytes_ -= kvobj_size(object);
                    if (replacement && table == 0) {
                        (void)track_expire(hash, replacement);
                        tab_[table][slot] = make_word(tag, replacement);
                        obj_bytes_ += kvobj_size(replacement);
                    } else {
                        untrack_expire(hash);
                        tab_[table][slot] = kTombBit;
                        live_[table]--; tombs_[table]++;
                    }
                    return object;
                }
                slot = (slot + 1) & mask_[table];
            }
            return nullptr;
        };
        auto insert_replacement = [&] {
            if (!replacement) return;
            if (!have_insertion_slot) std::abort();
            tab_[0][insertion_slot] = make_word(tag_of(hash), replacement);
            if (insertion_reuses_tomb) tombs_[0]--;
            live_[0]++;
            obj_bytes_ += kvobj_size(replacement);
            // Same tracker debt as the read-local twin: physical slot presence is not volatility.
            (void)track_expire(hash, replacement);
        };
        if (KvObj* object = exchange(0)) return object;
        if (rehashing()) {
            if (KvObj* object = exchange(1)) {
                insert_replacement();
                return object;
            }
        }
        insert_replacement();
        return nullptr;
    }

    bool atomic_recycle_value(KvObj* object) {
        if (!object || !atomic_pending_ || static_cast<Type>(object->type) != Type::String)
            return false;
        const Enc encoding = static_cast<Enc>(object->enc);
        if (encoding != Enc::Raw && encoding != Enc::Int) return false;
        if (encoding == Enc::Raw && outstanding_borrows_ && is_borrowed(object->str_data()))
            return false;
        const size_t allocation = kvobj_capacity(object);
        const uint32_t cls = atomic_pool_class(allocation);
        static constexpr size_t kValueCacheBytes = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
        if (cls >= AtomicPendingState::kPoolClasses ||
            allocation < sizeof(AtomicPendingState::FreeValue) ||
            atomic_pending_->cached_value_bytes + allocation > kValueCacheBytes) return false;
#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
        void* memory = object;
        std::destroy_at(object);
        auto* block = ::new (memory) AtomicPendingState::FreeValue{
            atomic_pending_->free_values[cls], allocation};
        // Only an actual key overlap whose commit tickets invert needs argmax collapse. Masks reject
        // almost all inverted entry pairs; when no such pair exists, the prefix reduces to freeing
        // parked predecessors and unlinking group entries. The usual monotonic case touches no key,
        // hash, table slot, or transient map.
        bool direct = true;
        uint64_t previous_epoch = 0;
        for (AtomicEntry* entry = atomic_pending_->head; entry != first_unselected;
             entry = entry->next) {
            if ((entry->group_epoch && entry->group_aborted &&
                 entry->group_aborted->load(std::memory_order_acquire)) ||
                atomic_epoch(*entry) < previous_epoch) {
                direct = false;
                break;
            }
            previous_epoch = atomic_epoch(*entry);
        }
        // Install order and ticket order are normally the same. Only an inversion needs the
        // pairwise membership/exact-key proof that the inverted entries do not overlap.
        if (!direct) {
            direct = true;
            for (AtomicEntry* later = atomic_pending_->head;
                 later != first_unselected && direct; later = later->next) {
                if (later->group_epoch && later->group_aborted &&
                    later->group_aborted->load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
                    direct = false;
                    break;
                }
                const uint64_t later_epoch = atomic_epoch(*later);
                for (AtomicEntry* earlier = atomic_pending_->head; earlier != later;
                     earlier = earlier->next) {
                    if (atomic_epoch(*earlier) <= later_epoch ||
                        !(earlier->membership & later->membership)) continue;
                    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < earlier->count && direct; i++) {
                        const uint64_t hash = atomic_entry_hash(*earlier, i);
                        if (!(later->membership & atomic_membership_bit(hash))) continue;
                        const Slice key = atomic_entry_key(*earlier, i);
                        for (uint32_t j = 0; j < later->count; j++) {
                            if (atomic_entry_hash(*later, j) == hash &&
                                atomic_entry_key(*later, j).key_eq(key)) {
                                direct = false;
                                break;
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    if (!direct) break;
                }
            }
        }
        if (direct) {
            atomic_pending_->cleanup_fast += occurrences;
            AtomicEntry* entry = atomic_pending_->head;
            while (entry != first_unselected) {
                AtomicEntry* next = entry->next;
                for (uint32_t i = 0; i < entry->count; i++) {
                    if (KvObj* parked = entry->parked()[i]) {
                        atomic_gauge_sub(kvobj_size(parked));
                        retire_detached_obj(parked);
                        entry->parked()[i] = nullptr;
                    }
                }
                // Grouped hashes live in ScatterState; close before its last owner pin can drop.
                read_local_pending_unpublish(*entry);
                if (entry->group_refs && (!entry->owner_refs || --*entry->owner_refs == 0))
                    entry->group_refs->fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_release);
                if (atomic_records_freed_) (*atomic_records_freed_)++;
                atomic_pending_->live--;
                atomic_unlink_conn(*entry);
                atomic_free_entry(entry);
                entry = next;
            }
            atomic_pending_->head = first_unselected;
            if (first_unselected) first_unselected->prev = nullptr;
            else atomic_pending_->tail = nullptr;
            if (!atomic_pending_->live && !atomic_pending_->script_intent_count &&
                atomic_activity_)
                atomic_activity_->fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_release);
            if (atomic_promotions_) *atomic_promotions_ += occurrences;
            return true;
        }

        // Detect overlap only inside the reclaimable prefix. A successor after the prefix already
        // parks the prefix's last installed candidate, so a committed non-overlapping entry needs
        // no table probe or chain surgery at all.
        bool overlap = false;
        uint64_t seen_bits = 0;
        if (occurrences > atomic_seen_keys_.max_size()) return false;
        try {
            atomic_seen_keys_.clear();
            atomic_seen_keys_.reserve(static_cast<size_t>(occurrences));
        } catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
            return false;
        }
        for (AtomicEntry* entry = atomic_pending_->head;
             entry != first_unselected && !overlap;
             entry = entry->next) {
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < entry->count; i++) {
                const uint64_t hash = atomic_entry_hash(*entry, i);
                const Slice key = atomic_entry_key(*entry, i);
                const uint64_t bit = atomic_membership_bit(hash);
                if (seen_bits & bit) {
                    for (const AtomicSeenKey& seen : atomic_seen_keys_) {
                        if (seen.hash == hash && seen.key.key_eq(key)) {
                            overlap = true;
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                }
                if (overlap) break;
                atomic_seen_keys_.push_back(AtomicSeenKey{hash, key});
                seen_bits |= bit;
            }
        }
        if (!overlap) {
            atomic_pending_->cleanup_slow += occurrences;
            uint64_t promoted = 0;
            AtomicEntry* entry = atomic_pending_->head;
            while (entry != first_unselected) {
                AtomicEntry* next = entry->next;
                const bool aborted = entry->group_epoch && entry->group_aborted &&
                    entry->group_aborted->load(std::memory_order_acquire);
                for (uint32_t i = 0; i < entry->count; i++) {
                    const uint64_t hash = atomic_entry_hash(*entry, i);
                    const Slice key = atomic_entry_key(*entry, i);
                    KvObj* parked = entry->parked()[i];
                    if (aborted) {
                        KvObj* replacement = atomic_live_value(parked);
                        AtomicEntry* boundary = nullptr;
                        uint32_t boundary_index = 0;
                        const uint64_t bit = atomic_membership_bit(hash);
                        for (AtomicEntry* scan = first_unselected; scan && !boundary;
                             scan = scan->next) {
                            if (!(scan->membership & bit)) continue;
                            for (uint32_t j = 0; j < scan->count; j++) {
                                if (atomic_entry_hash(*scan, j) == hash &&
                                    atomic_entry_key(*scan, j).key_eq(key)) {
                                    boundary = scan;
                                    boundary_index = j;
                                    break;
                                }
                            }
                        }
                        if (boundary) {
                            KvObj* loser = boundary->parked()[boundary_index];
                            if (loser) atomic_gauge_sub(kvobj_size(loser));
                            if (loser != replacement) retire_detached_obj(loser);
                            boundary->parked()[boundary_index] = replacement;
                            if (parked && parked != replacement) {
                                atomic_gauge_sub(kvobj_size(parked));
                                retire_detached_obj(parked);
                            }
                        } else {
                            KvObj* physical = atomic_find_physical(hash, key);
                            if (physical != replacement) {
                                if (__builtin_expect(atomic_tripwire_enabled(), false))
                                    atomic_tripwire_collapse_write(hash, physical == nullptr,
                                                                   replacement == nullptr,
                                                                   atomic_epoch(*entry));
                                KvObj* loser = atomic_exchange_physical(hash, key, replacement);
                                if (loser != physical) std::abort();
                                retire_detached_obj(loser);
                            }
                            if (parked) {
                                atomic_gauge_sub(kvobj_size(parked));
                                if (parked != replacement) retire_detached_obj(parked);
                            }
                        }
                    } else if (parked) {
                        atomic_gauge_sub(kvobj_size(parked));
                        retire_detached_obj(parked);
                    }
                    entry->parked()[i] = nullptr;
                    promoted++;
                }
                // Grouped hashes live in ScatterState; close before its last owner pin can drop.

// flatstore.h — the keyspace table. Replaces Redis's dict/kvstore (NOT its RDB, which is a
// persistence format we have not built).
//
// ONE TABLE PER SHARD, executed by exactly one worker at a time. In the fork the table was per-NODE
// and shared by several workers, which forced it to be lock-free with QSBR — not because ownership
// was shared (it never was; ownership is per key) but because open addressing lets worker A's probe
// walk through slots holding worker B's keys. One table per shard removes that whole class of
// problem: no atomics, no CAS, no epoch reclamation, no probe interference.
//
// ============================================================================================
// WHAT IS NEVER COPIED, AND WHAT MOVES
//
//   KvObj (key + value bytes)   NEVER copied and NEVER moved, by anything, ever. A key's storage is
//                               allocated once and freed once. Every operation below moves at most
//                               an 8-byte slot word that POINTS at it.
//
//   Shard migration (LB)        moves NOTHING AT ALL. Reassigning a shard rewrites only the EX bits
//                               in Router's bucket entries behind one descriptor commit. No table
//                               is touched, no pointer is rehashed. Pure ownership handoff.
//
//   Table resize                rehashes 8-byte SLOT WORDS into a larger or smaller array, because
//                               an open-addressed slot index is a function of the capacity. This is
//                               pointer movement, not data movement — the objects those pointers
//                               name do not budge.
//
// ============================================================================================
// RESIZE IS INCREMENTAL. NOTHING STOPS THE WORLD.
//
// Rehashing a large table in one pass is a multi-second stall on the write tail — the fork measured
// exactly that and had to move to serve-while-copy to turn a 2.4 s p99.99 into 39 ms. So this works
// the way Redis's dict does: allocate the new table, keep the old one, and migrate a BOUNDED number
// of slots on every subsequent operation. No operation pays more than that bound, so the tail stays
// flat while the table grows underneath the workload.
//
//   t_[0]  the CURRENT table. Every insert goes here. Always present.
//   t_[1]  the OLD table, present only while rehashing. Drains, then is freed.
//
// THE RESURRECTION HAZARD, easy to get wrong and silently wrong. A key can still sit in the old
// table when a new value for it is inserted into the current one. Delete the current copy and the
// old one becomes visible again — the key returns from the dead. So insert evicts any old-table copy
// first, and erase checks both tables. Exactly ONE copy of a key exists at any instant, which is the
// invariant every lookup depends on.
// ============================================================================================
//
// SLOT ENCODING — one 8-byte word, eight slots per cache line:
//
//   [63:49] 15-bit tag   high bits of the hash; rejects a non-matching probe without touching the key
//   [48]    TOMB
//   [47:0]  KvObj*       boot verifies the allocator stays in the low 48-bit VA range; debug packs
//                       assert the same invariant before using the top bits
//
//   word == 0             EMPTY  the calloc state, and the ONLY thing that stops a probe
//   ptr != 0              LIVE
//   word != 0, ptr == 0   DEAD   tombstone; reusable, never stops a probe
//
// THE CLUSTERING TRAP, kept because it cost real time: the router consumes the LOW bits of the same
// hash that indexes this table. Index with `h & mask` and the routing bits are frozen for every key
// a shard owns — only 1/nshards of slots are natural homes, and linear probing degenerates into
// kilo-slot runs. Measured at ~6,600 probes per lookup. slot_start() mixes again before taking the
// index; that alone was worth 2.5-2.7x.
#pragma once
#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <cassert>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>

#include <memory>
#include <new>

              TOMO_READ_LOCAL_RECLAIM_PREFETCHW == 1,
              "TOMO_READ_LOCAL_RECLAIM_PREFETCHW must be 0 (off) or 1 (on)");
inline constexpr bool kReadLocalReclaimPrefetchw =
    TOMO_READ_LOCAL_RECLAIM_PREFETCHW != 0;

// Fault injection for the cold table-allocation paths. It is compiled in whenever NDEBUG is not
// defined -- which is every build the Makefile produces, release included -- and costs one relaxed
// load per table allocation, never anything on the request path. Defining NDEBUG removes this
// surface (and every assert() in the tree) as a build-system decision.
#ifndef NDEBUG
inline std::atomic<uint32_t> g_flatstore_table_alloc_failures{0};

inline void flatstore_debug_fail_table_allocations(uint32_t count) {
    g_flatstore_table_alloc_failures.store(count, std::memory_order_relaxed);
}

inline bool flatstore_debug_consume_table_alloc_failure() {
    uint32_t remaining = g_flatstore_table_alloc_failures.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    while (remaining) {
        if (g_flatstore_table_alloc_failures.compare_exchange_weak(
                remaining, remaining - 1, std::memory_order_relaxed)) return true;
    }
    return false;
}
#endif

inline void* flatstore_table_calloc(size_t count, size_t width) {
#ifndef NDEBUG
    if (flatstore_debug_consume_table_alloc_failure()) return nullptr;
#endif
    return std::calloc(count, width);
}

inline uint64_t mix64(uint64_t h);

// Expiring hashes only, not keys or object pointers: object replacement never invalidates this
// index. State is a byte sidecar so all 64-bit hash values remain representable while occupied
// slots themselves stay densely packed. Sampling advances a persistent cursor and examines at most
// its caller's budget, including empty slots; no pass can accidentally turn into a keyspace walk.
//
// GROWTH AND SHRINK ARE BOTH BOUNDED PER OPERATION, for the same reason the main table's are:
//   - Growth moves at most kMigrateSlotsPerOp old slots per operation into a second table, exactly
//     the two-table shape FlatStore::rehash_step() already uses. A single-pass move of a million
//     deadlines stalled its owning executor -- and therefore its whole shard -- for tens of
//     milliseconds inside one ordinary SET.
//   - Reaching zero live deadlines RELEASES the sidecar instead of clearing every state byte. The
//     old clear was O(capacity) on a transition a workload can hit on every key, and capacity was
//     monotone in the all-time-high volatile population, so one historical burst taxed every later
//     live->0 forever. Releasing is O(1) and makes the footprint follow the CURRENT population.
// A table at or below the minimum keeps its buffer and clears the 16 state bytes, so the ordinary
// "a few volatile keys come and go" case stays allocation-free.
class ExpireIndex {
public:
    ExpireIndex() = default;
    ~ExpireIndex() { std::free(hashes_[0]); std::free(sidecars_[0]);
                     std::free(hashes_[1]); std::free(sidecars_[1]); }
    ExpireIndex(const ExpireIndex&) = delete;
    ExpireIndex& operator=(const ExpireIndex&) = delete;

    uint32_t size() const { return live_[0] + live_[1]; }
    // A move in flight is PENDING WORK for the owner, not a quiet background state: half the
    // index is parked in the old table, and an owner that sleeps on a barren sampling pass stops
    // expiring until the next command wakes it.
    bool migrating() const { return cap_[1] != 0; }
    size_t memory_bytes() const {
        return static_cast<size_t>((static_cast<uint64_t>(cap_[0]) + cap_[1]) *
                                   (sizeof(uint64_t) + sizeof(uint8_t) +
                                    (kTtlDeadlineSidecar ? sizeof(int64_t) : 0)));
    }
    void clear() {
        release(0);
        release(1);
        cursor_ = 0;
        migrate_ = 0;
    }

    bool insert(uint64_t hash, int64_t deadline = kNoTtlDeadline) {
        if (rehashing()) {

            // Backstop only. At the shipped step rate the new table is at most ~41% loaded when the
            // move ends, so this cannot fire; finishing the move is still cheaper than letting an
            // insert run out of slots.
            if (rehashing() &&
                (static_cast<uint64_t>(live_[1]) + tombs_[1] + 1) * 100 >=
                    static_cast<uint64_t>(cap_[1]) * 70)
                finish_migration();
        }
        if (!cap_[0] && !allocate(0, kMinCap)) return false;
        if (!rehashing() &&
            (static_cast<uint64_t>(live_[0]) + tombs_[0] + 1) * 100 >=
                static_cast<uint64_t>(cap_[0]) * 70) {
            uint64_t wanted = cap_[0];
            if (static_cast<uint64_t>(live_[0]) * 2 >= cap_[0]) {
                if (wanted > std::numeric_limits<size_t>::max() / uint64_t{2}) return false;
                wanted *= uint64_t{2};

    bool erase(uint64_t hash) {

    int64_t deadline(uint64_t hash, int64_t fallback) const {
